summary: Bouncer on a 10-background with domain walls; self-similar epochs a'=3a+6, c'=3a+c+2 (exact, 5/5)
mechanism: Tape = alternating 10 background plus a few walls (00, 11, (010)^2, dense 1011 blocks).
Sweeps flip 10<->01 and bounce off walls; phases (fixed sweep programs) chain into epochs, span x3 per epoch.
Epoch anchors P(a,c,T): a' = 3a+6, c' = 3a+c+2 exactly. The tail rule T -> T' is the open question.

template.diff: 12/12 transitions differ (8/12 after best mirror+renaming); Bouncer_v3.v TM1: 11/12 (9/12)
template.note:
No rule or config carries over (from LongNv1 TM1's start ours halts in 3 steps).
The technique does: segRLs_n history induction P n -> P (S n) fits our x3 epoch induction.

strategy:
Per-phase cycle lemmas (es + ind), chained with follow into Epoch: P(a,c,T) -->+ P(3a+6,3a+c+2,T').
Then induct over epochs with progress_nonhalt_cond (invariant: a even, c odd, Inv(T)).
Inv(T) = tail language closed under one epoch, via Longitudinal sideRLs/segRLs_n (Bouncer_v3, LongNv1) or LongN closed sets.
risks: Tail T is rewritten every epoch (73-100% of it is read); its rule T->T' is unknown and may be chaotic.
Each epoch has many 5-7-counter phases; a hand proof could exceed 50 KB.
Halt pattern D> 1^k 00 exists and the tail has 0^2/0^3 walls; non-halting depends on the tail invariant.
